source_files.license: Doc2Present dataset card MIT; embedded third-party figure reuse permission not independently verified
claims: Conventional video compression approaches use the predictive coding architecture and encode the corresponding motion information and residual information.

In this paper, taking advantage of both classical architecture in the conventional video compression method and the powerful nonlinear representation ability of neural networks, we propose the first end-to-end video compression deep model that jointly optimizes all the components for video compression.

figures.caption: Visual quality of the reconstructed frames from different video compression systems. (a) is the original frame. (b)-(d) are the reconstructed frames from H.264, H.265 and our method. Our proposed method only consumes 0.0529pp while achieving the best perceptual quality (0.961) when measured by MS-SSIM. (Best viewed in color.)

source_files.filename: Factorized and Controllable Neural Re-Rendering of Outdoor Scene for Photo Extrapolation.pdf
source_files.license: Doc2Present dataset card MIT; embedded third-party figure reuse permission not independently verified
claims: Expanding an existing tourist photo from a partially captured scene to a full scene is one of the desired experiences for photography applications.

Although photo extrapolation has been well studied, it is much more challenging to extrapolate a photo (i.e., selfie) from a narrow field of view to a wider one while maintaining a similar visual style.

figures.caption: Given an Internet photo collection of an outdoor attraction, we learn a novel neural re-rendering model that encodes scenes with several factorized components, which enables the applicabilities of controllable scene re-rendering, photo extrapolation and extrapolated 3D photo generation (see GIF in Fig. 7). All the images are from the IMC-PT dataset [14]. Photos by Flickr users astrobri, soniadal82, Fotero, scriptingnews, Devin Ford, and MikiAnn.
